title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: how many free-time records a customer and a container may hold
content:
## Scope

This policy of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category governs the opening of per-container free-time records: how many records a customer may hold and when a second record for the same container is refused.

## Policy clauses

1. A customer holds one free-time record for every container on every leg it is billed for. There is no cap on the number of records a customer may hold.
2. Each container of a booking has at most one record per direction (import or export).
3. A second record for the same container, the same booking and the same direction is never opened.
4. A container that moves again under another booking gets a record under that booking.

## Basis of the one-record check

- The check is made against the line's own records before the record is opened; a customer's statement does not replace it.
- The three items that identify the leg are the booking, the container number and the direction, and all three must match the record being opened.
- An existing record counts against the new one when its status is one of exactly these: free time running, charges accruing, clock stopped, invoiced or settled.

## Input, judgement, output

> **Input**: the booking, the container number and the direction of the leg to be opened.
> **Judgement**: does a record already exist for that same booking, container and direction in one of the counting statuses above?
> **Output**: where it does, no second record is opened; the existing record stands for that leg.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Container A is on booking B, and a record for the import leg of A on B is already free time running; an import record for A on B is requested again | Not opened, clause 3 |
| Container A on booking B already has an import record; its export leg on the same booking has none | The export record may be opened, since the direction differs |
| Container A had a settled record under booking B and now moves under booking C | A record is opened under booking C, clause 4 |
| A customer already holds a large number of records across many bookings | No count limit applies, clause 1 |
